description: Experiment under experiments/branch-coverage proving that Istanbul instrumentation served through a Bun preload plugin yields per-file branch coverage (BRDA/BRF/BRH) in lcov.info for the constructs crow uses: standard decorators before export, using, TSX, import attributes, import.meta.dirname. notes: Run 2026-10-14 on Bun 1.4.3 via experiments/branch-coverage/run.sh: all criteria pass. Criterion 1: instrument.ts instrumented 7 files, Babel re-printed the standard decorator before export, using, TSX and import attributes, and Bun.Transpiler accepted every result. Criterion 2: spike test 11 pass with and without the preload. Criterion 3: SF records for all 7 fixtures including unloaded.ts seeded with LF=3 LH=0. Criterion 4: branches.ts BRF=8 BRH=7, the only unhit BRDA is line 6 block 2 index 2 (the switch default case, Istanbul reports all cases on the switch line). Criterion 5: decorators.ts BRF=2 BRH=2. Criterion 6: Bun control lcov has 60 DA, 0 BRDA, 0 BRF. Criterion 7: instrumented run 0 s wall-clock for 11 tests, too small to extrapolate. Also agents/check-coverage consumed the Istanbul lcov unchanged and flagged branches.ts branches at 87 percent and unloaded.ts at 0 percent, as expected. Finding: Bun omits the frame of the function that constructed an Error even without instrumentation, so the planned error-stack probe was replaced by import.meta.path. Gate change: Exec(bun) and Exec(experiments/branch-coverage/run.sh) added to .devin/config.json so Claude can run it.
